record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: What asymptotic conditions allow the conformal method to construct initial data sets on asymptotically hyperbolic manifolds, such as constant-mean-curvature hypersurfaces meeting future null infinity, also called hyperboloidal initial data sets?

evidence.quote: Describe suitable asymptotic conditions which enable the conformal method to be used to construct initial data sets on an asymptotically hyperbolic manifold (eg. a CMC hypersurface meeting ~+). Such initial data sets are called hyperboloidal.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g,K)$ denote a Riemannian 3-manifold $M$ with metric $g$ and symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor $K$ satisfying the vacuum Einstein constraint equations
$$R_g - |K|_g^2 + (\operatorname{tr}_g K)^2 = 0, \qquad \operatorname{div}_g K - d(\operatorname{tr}_g K) = 0,$$
where $R_g$ is the scalar curvature of $g$. Such a triple is called an initial data set. An initial data set is called hyperboloidal (or asymptotically hyperboloidal) if $(M,g)$ is an asymptotically hyperbolic 3-manifold and $K$ models the extrinsic curvature of a constant-mean-curvature spacelike hypersurface meeting future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$ in an asymptotically simple spacetime; in particular $\operatorname{tr}_g K$ is (asymptotically) constant and nonzero.

The conformal method seeks to construct solutions of the constraint equations by prescribing a conformal class $[\tilde g]$ on $M$, a mean curvature function $\tau$, and a transverse-traceless tensor $\sigma$ as free data, and then solving the conformal constraint system (the Lichnerowicz equation coupled with the conformal vector Laplacian equation) for a conformal factor $\phi>0$ and a vector field $W$ so that
$$g = \phi^4 \tilde g, \qquad K = \phi^{-2}\bigl(\sigma + \tfrac12 \mathcal{L}_{\tilde g} W\bigr) + \tfrac{\tau}{3} g.$$

Problem: Identify and describe explicit asymptotic conditions on the free data $(\tilde g, \tau, \sigma)$ at the conformal boundary of an asymptotically hyperbolic manifold $M$ under which the conformal method produces hyperboloidal initial data sets, i.e., yields solutions $(g,K)$ of the vacuum Einstein constraints possessing the asymptotic geometry of a smooth (or polyhomogeneous) CMC hypersurface meeting future null infinity. Characterize, in particular, the conditions on the free data that ensure the resulting initial data admit a smooth conformal compactification free of logarithmic singularities at $\mathscr{I}^+$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been the subject of substantial progress but is not fully resolved. Andersson–Chruściel–Friedrich and subsequent work showed that generic solutions of the conformal constraint equations on asymptotically hyperbolic manifolds admit only polyhomogeneous expansions and exhibit logarithmic singularities at the conformal boundary; only a non-generic subclass of free data yields smooth conformal compactifications. Recent results (e.g., on the parabolic-hyperbolic formulation and 2025 work on hyperboloidal initial data without logarithmic singularities) provide further sufficient asymptotic conditions, but a complete classification of asymptotic conditions on the conformal free data guaranteeing hyperboloidal initial data sets remains open.

status_evidence.title: Hyperboloidal initial data without logarithmic singularities
status_evidence.snippet: Generic asymptotically hyperboloidal initial data sets admit polyhomogeneous expansions, and only a non-generic subclass of solutions of the conformal constraint equations is free of logarithmic singularities.
status_evidence.claim: Conformal method generically produces logarithmic singularities; smoothness requires special asymptotic conditions, indicating only partial resolution.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotically hyperboloidal initial data sets from a parabolic-hyperbolic formulation of the Einstein vacuum constraints
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of well-defined Bondi mass and angular momentum, together with mild restrictions on the free data, implies that generic solutions of the parabolic-hyperbolic form are completely free of logarithmic singularities.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial progress identifies asymptotic conditions ensuring smooth hyperboloidal initial data sets.

status_evidence.title: Conformal Infinity
status_evidence.snippet: The conformal approach based on the hyperboloidal initial-value problem... has matured enough to provide an approach to applications in numerical relativity.
status_evidence.claim: The conformal method on hyperboloidal slices is developed but asymptotic conditions remain a subject of active research.
